Upon studying at Queen's Academy, she earned top honors in the domestic science course.

There was no ciphering her out by the rules that worked with other children. It’s nothing short of wonderful how she’s improved these three years, but especially in looks. She managed her house, ran the local Sewing Circle, helped run the Sunday school, and served as a strong leader in the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. When Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert decided to adopt an orphan boy, Rachel visited Green Gables out of curiosity. Later, upon meeting Anne Shirley, Rachel bluntness about Anne's looks provoked an angry outburst from the child. Though outraged at the insult, Rachel maintained her neighborly ties with Marilla and offered counsel on child-rearing. She also advised Marilla when Anne ran into trouble with schoolmaster Mr. Phillips. As an ardent Liberal, she attended a political rally in Charlottetown even though the speaking Premier was a Conservative. Over the years, Rachel admitted she had been mistaken about Anne, praising her dramatic improvement and achievements despite her continued disapproval of higher education for women.
